title: THREAD LOGIC — A touring exhibition of textile archives and digital weaving, 14 deliverables

config.text:
# THREAD LOGIC

## Identity
- Exhibition name: THREAD LOGIC
- Entrance, video and presentation phrase: From fibre to code
- Sections, in visit order: Fibre; Repeat; Code
- Collection: four original textiles, T01–T04
- Dimensions of each original: 600 × 400 mm, width × height
- Section assignments: T01 / Fibre; T02 / Repeat; T03 and T04 / Code
- T03 pattern: 50 mm squares, 12 columns × 8 rows
- T04 pattern: 25 mm squares, 24 columns × 16 rows

## Display conditions
- Flat textile cases: 4
- Textile support height: 800 mm above floor
- Case top height: 850 mm above floor
- Label centre height: 900 mm above floor
- Graphic support height: 1800 mm above floor
- Original textile illumination limit: 50 lux
- Separate label illumination: 150 lux
- Label body type: 24 pt
- Object title length limit: 6 words
- Object body length limit: 45 words
- Teaching replicas: R01 and R02, each 150 × 150 mm
- Touch ledge height: 800 mm above floor
- R01 position: beside T01 in Fibre
- R02 position: beside T04 in Code
- Original access: enclosed display
- Teaching replica access: visitor touch
- Digital display: one 13-inch screen in Code

## Touring furniture
- Frame material: aluminium
- Support material: birch plywood
- Enclosure material: removable acrylic panels
- Connections: M6 bolts
- Assembly tool: 5 mm hex key
- Maximum detached part envelope: 850 × 600 × 80 mm
- Transport crates: C1, C2, C3
- C1–C2 contents: furniture, graphics, screen, teaching replicas and installation accessories
- C3 contents: four padded original-textile trays
- Textile trays: four, each 700 × 500 × 40 mm externally
- Textile travel orientation: flat

## Venues and visitors
- Loom Hall clear dimensions: 10000 × 8000 × 3000 mm, east–west × south–north × height
- Shuttle Room clear dimensions: 8000 × 6000 × 2700 mm, east–west × south–north × height
- Visitor entrance at each venue: south wall, 1400 mm clear width
- Visitor exit at each venue: east wall, 1400 mm clear width
- Reserved circulation: 1200 mm strips along south and east walls
- Host furniture: two visitor seats per venue
- Visit duration: 20 minutes
- Concurrent visitors: 12
- Audience: general public and design students interested in hand weaving and digital patterning
- Working recipients: archive team, exhibition fabricator and host venues

## Collection and transport records
- Object records, label bodies, touch labels and screen captions: 03-collection.md
- Opening coordinates, loading access, lifts and crate dimensions: 04-tour-logistics.md

| 7 | interpretation-artwork | Interpretation artwork | 14 | Format: presentation document; at least eight actual pages. Stage: final. |
| 8 | screen-storyboard | Digital weaving screen storyboard | 14 | Format: PNG, 1920 by 1080 proportion, long side at least 1024 pixels. Stage: final. |
| 9 | loom-hall-view | Loom Hall entrance perspective | 14 | Format: PNG, 1800 by 1200 proportion, long side at least 1024 pixels. Stage: final. |

# Collection records

## Original textiles

| ID | Title | Year | Material | Technique | Width × height | Section | Appearance |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| T01 | Linen Ground | 1984 | Undyed linen | Handwoven plain weave | 600 × 400 mm | Fibre | Oatmeal field; visible alternating over-one, under-one intersections; straight bound edges |
| T02 | Twill Study | 1992 | Cotton | Handwoven 2/2 twill | 600 × 400 mm | Repeat | Navy warp and ecru weft; fine diagonals rising from lower left to upper right; straight bound edges |
| T03 | Card Check | 2006 | Cotton | Punched-card Jacquard weaving | 600 × 400 mm | Code | Rust and ecru checkerboard; 50 mm squares; 12 columns × 8 rows; rust upper-left square; straight bound edges |
| T04 | Digital Check | 2024 | Cotton | Electronic Jacquard weaving | 600 × 400 mm | Code | Navy and ecru checkerboard; 25 mm squares; 24 columns × 16 rows; navy upper-left square; straight bound edges |

## Object label copy

| ID | Title | Year line | Body |
|---|---|---|---|
| T01 | Linen Ground | 1984 | Undyed linen, handwoven in plain weave. Each weft passes over one warp thread and under the next. The alternating intersections give this sample its even surface. |
| T02 | Twill Study | 1992 | Cotton, handwoven in a two-over, two-under twill. Each row shifts the sequence by one thread, producing the diagonal visible across the cloth. |
| T03 | Card Check | 2006 | Cotton, woven on a punched-card Jacquard loom. The card sequence selects warp threads for lifting. Rust and ecru squares repeat every 50 mm across this sample. |
| T04 | Digital Check | 2024 | Cotton, woven on an electronic Jacquard loom. A digital pattern file controls warp selection. Navy and ecru squares repeat every 25 mm; warp and weft still form the cloth. |

## Section names

| Order | Name | Original IDs |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Fibre | T01 |
| 2 | Repeat | T02 |
| 3 | Code | T03, T04 |

## Teaching replicas

| ID | Source | Dimensions | Material and structure | Position | Label title | Label body | Access |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| R01 | T01 | 150 × 150 mm | Undyed linen, plain weave | Beside T01 in Fibre | R01 — Touch sample | Teaching replica of T01. Feel the alternating plain-weave intersections. | Visitor touch |
| R02 | T04 | 150 × 150 mm | Cotton, navy and ecru 25 mm checkerboard, 6 columns × 6 rows | Beside T04 in Code | R02 — Touch sample | Teaching replica of T04. Feel the woven surface beneath the digital pattern. | Visitor touch |

## Screen sequence

| Frame | Linked objects | Exact caption | Visual subject |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | T03 | T03: Punched cards select warp threads for lifting. | Card sequence and selected warp threads |
| 2 | T04 | T04: A digital pattern file controls warp selection. | Digital pattern grid and selected warp threads |
| 3 | T03, T04 | Both samples form cloth by interlacing warp and weft. | Shared warp-and-weft structure beside the two samples |

## Public identity copy

| Element | Text |
|---|---|
| Exhibition name | THREAD LOGIC |
| Exhibition phrase | From fibre to code |

steps.userMessage:
THREAD LOGIC | A touring exhibition of textile archives and digital weaving

We are taking four archive textiles into small venues where visitors can follow the relationship between fibre, woven structure and digital pattern control. Build the exhibition around T01–T04, each 600 × 400 mm, and the three sections Fibre, Repeat and Code. T01 belongs to Fibre, T02 to Repeat, and T03–T04 to Code. Preserve the textile patterns in the attached collection images, including T03's 12 × 8 checkerboard and T04's 24 × 16 checkerboard. Print "THREAD LOGIC" and "From fibre to code" on the entrance graphic, video and presentation. Each object's ID, title and year travel together on the plans, object labels and presentation collection pages.

The same kit must fit Loom Hall, 10000 × 8000 mm with 3000 mm clear height, and Shuttle Room, 8000 × 6000 mm with 2700 mm clear height. Both have a 1400 mm south entrance, a 1400 mm east exit and reserved 1200 mm clear strips along the south and east walls. The logistics table fixes their loading doors, lifts and three transport crates. Develop four flat textile cases using aluminium frames, birch plywood supports and removable acrylic panels, with M6 bolts operated by a 5 mm hex key. Detached parts fit within 850 × 600 × 80 mm. Original textiles travel flat in four padded trays in C3; furniture, graphics and the single 13-inch screen travel in C1–C2. Set textile supports at 800 mm, case tops at 850 mm, label centres at 900 mm and graphic supports at 1800 mm. Originals have a 50 lux lighting limit; separately lit labels use 150 lux and 24 pt body text. Two 150 × 150 mm teaching replicas, R01 and R02, sit on touch ledges at 800 mm beside T01 and T04 respectively. The screen explains the supplied card-to-digital sequence. Each venue supplies two visitor seats. Plan for a 20-minute visit and 12 visitors at a time.

Audience: the archive team, exhibition fabricator and host venues will use the work to approve the touring kit and arrange its installation for the public and design students.

Inputs (attached): 01-client-facts.en.md contains the fixed exhibition identity, display conditions and visitor brief. 02-delivery-catalog.en.md lists the deliverables, proportions, formats and stages. 03-collection.md contains the object records, exact label copy, teaching replicas and screen text. 04-tour-logistics.md contains venue boundaries, opening positions, lift dimensions and crate records. venue-and-transport.png diagrams the fixed spaces and transport envelopes. textile-fronts.png records all four textile faces and their proportions. textile-details.png records their weave structures and pattern repeats. empty-gallery.png provides the atmosphere of a small, unoccupied host venue.

Deliverables:
1. One two-page collection and route schedule, with T01–T04 IDs, titles, years, dimensions, section assignments, visit order and the four installation heights
2. One label copy schedule, with four object titles and bodies, three section names, two touch labels and three screen captions; object titles limited to six words and bodies to 45 words
3. Two dimensioned visitor route plans, one per venue, with collection positions, section names, circulation widths, seats and the screen
4. One elevation and section sheet covering all four cases, label mounting, graphic supports, touch ledges and lighting positions
5. One furniture and packing document, with assembled and exploded drawings, a numbered component inventory, material thicknesses, joint details and a complete allocation to C1–C3
6. One six-page interpretation artwork document: an entrance graphic and three section headers on page 1, one object label on each of pages 2–5, and both touch labels on page 6
7. One three-frame screen storyboard linking the T03 card record, T04 digital record and their shared warp-control principle
8. Two visitor perspectives, one from Loom Hall's south entrance and one from Shuttle Room's east exit looking toward Code
9. Two installation-state drawings for Shuttle Room, one during assembly and one after dismantling with the three crates open
10. One 10-second exhibition video moving from the entrance through Fibre, Repeat and Code to the two teaching replicas
11. One presentation document of at least 10 pages, reusing the schedules, plans, furniture drawings, interpretation, storyboard and perspectives, with collection pages and a touring-facts index naming the deliverable and page or view where each fixed fact appears

Acceptance:
- The collection and route schedule assigns T01 to Fibre, T02 to Repeat and T03–T04 to Code; both route plans and the presentation repeat those assignments, the 600 × 400 mm object dimensions, and every object's ID, title and year from 03-collection.md.
- Both route plans dimension the stated venue boundaries, 1400 mm visitor openings and 1200 mm reserved circulation strips, and locate four cases, two touch ledges, one screen and two seats. The elevation sheet, visitor perspectives and installation-state drawings use those same positions for the venue shown.
- The collection and route schedule, elevation sheet and presentation repeat the 800 mm textile support, 850 mm case top, 900 mm label centre and 1800 mm graphic support heights. The elevation sheet and interpretation artwork identify 24 pt label body text; the elevation sheet marks 50 lux at originals and 150 lux at separately lit labels, with shielding drawn between the two lighting areas.
- The furniture and packing document counts each component type, identifies aluminium, birch plywood, acrylic and M6 joints, and dimensions every detached part within 850 × 600 × 80 mm. Its crate layouts and the dismantled-state drawing account for the complete kit inside the three usable crate envelopes in 04-tour-logistics.md, with four 700 × 500 × 40 mm textile trays in C3; the assembly drawing identifies the 5 mm hex-key connections.
- The label copy schedule and interpretation artwork reproduce the object titles and bodies, section names and touch labels in 03-collection.md exactly, within the six-word title and 45-word body limits. The storyboard repeats all three supplied screen captions in order. The entrance artwork, video and presentation print THREAD LOGIC and From fibre to code.
- The visitor perspectives, video and presentation preserve the four textile faces, including T03's 12 × 8 and T04's 24 × 16 checkerboards, and place R01 beside T01 and R02 beside T04. The video runs for 10 seconds; the presentation contains at least 10 pages and locates the schedules' collection records, section names and installation heights in its touring-facts index.

Please clearly mark which version you consider the final deliverable. If nothing is marked, the last exported version counts.
